presentationRules: Dock meets canyon under attack by swarms of pulse units.
Dynamic traversal featuring dark industrial dock tones contrasted against stark canyon landscapes, enhanced by colorful pulse effects and sharp spike animations.
mustPreserve: Preserve the randomized seed contract through every stage.

Keep the generated game self-contained in one Pages/<slug>/ folder.

stageHistory.summary: Materialized concept from locked brainstorm packet.
Derived feature sprint packets from canonical brainstorm data.
Derived fun assessment and implementation chapters.
Created story payload and runtime scaffold for stealth_patrol.
Pass 1 should repair the generic relic arena into a relay-repair courier loop before deeper enemy or hazard work.
Pass 2 should lock one commander archetype so the relay run has route-control pressure and a readable pulse counter-window.

decisions: Keep the existing three.js scaffold and patch mechanics locally.
Use Movement as the active packet because it best changes player feel immediately.
Delay commander and finale work until the relay loop is playable.
Use One Enemy Archetype as the second and final initial planning pass.
Model the commander as a lane-control threat rather than a high-health brute.
Advance out of Stage 8 after this pass so live file implementation and validation can happen.
rejectedIdeas: Do not rewrite the entire runtime in the first implementation pass.
Do not add broad new systems that are not needed for the relay loop.
Do not add multiple new enemy classes in this pass.
Do not spend this pass on broad visual polish instead of route pressure.
openIssues: Current scaffold copy and mechanics still mention relic collection and exit unlocking.
The generated overlay hint currently includes raw UI note text instead of a cleaned control summary.
The actual runtime files still need the relay and commander edits applied.
A route hazard pass may still be needed if the arena floor remains too static in play.
nextStageNotes: Validation should explicitly check that relic wording is gone from the playable loop.
Arcade integration should only proceed after one browser smoke pass confirms the relay run is readable and playable.
Validation should check for relay wording, commander pressure, and pulse counterplay in the live runtime.
If the game still feels generic after browser smoke testing, use the validation loop to justify one hazard-focused repair pass.
